record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: Are there general principles that determine which renormalization-group domain wall or conformal boundary state is selected from the set of possible interfaces or boundary states connecting the ultraviolet and infrared endpoints of a renormalization-group flow in boundary or defect conformal field theory?

evidence.quote: Are there general principles that select the RG domain wall(s)/boundary state(s) from the possible set connecting the UV and IR endpoints of RG flows?

artifact.category_tag: RG domain walls in boundary/defect CFT
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let a renormalization-group (RG) flow connect an ultraviolet (UV) conformal field theory CFT_UV to an infrared (IR) conformal field theory CFT_IR, triggered by a relevant deformation. To such a flow one can associate codimension-one conformal interfaces (RG domain walls) between CFT_UV and CFT_IR, or, equivalently via the folding trick, conformal boundary states in the product theory CFT_UV ⊗ \\overline{CFT_IR}. In general there are many conformal interfaces (or boundary states) compatible with the symmetries and gluing conditions linking the UV and IR endpoints.

Problem: Formulate and establish general principles (for example, based on entropy/g-theorem minimization, unitarity, locality, symmetry preservation, modular/Cardy-type consistency conditions, or variational characterizations of the flow) that uniquely determine, or at least canonically select, the RG domain wall (equivalently, the conformal boundary state) associated with a given RG flow from the set of all conformal interfaces between CFT_UV and CFT_IR. In particular, give a criterion that picks out the physically realized RG interface and prove it characterizes the interface uniquely in nontrivial families of examples (e.g., flows between minimal models in two dimensions, or between higher-dimensional boundary/defect CFTs).
artifact.status_search_result: The question of identifying a general selection principle for RG domain walls or boundary states associated to RG flows in boundary/defect CFT is widely regarded as open. Partial constructions exist in two-dimensional examples (e.g., Gaiotto's RG interfaces between Virasoro minimal models, and proposals using boundary entropy/g-theorem considerations), but no general principle has been established. Recent reviews of boundary/defect CFT list this as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Gaiotto, Domain walls for two-dimensional renormalization group flows
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs RG domain walls between coset minimal models, providing examples but not a general selection principle.
status_evidence.claim: Specific constructions of RG interfaces exist in 2d minimal-model flows, but the general selection question remains.

status_evidence.title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems including identifying principles selecting RG domain walls/boundary states connecting UV and IR fixed points.
status_evidence.claim: Selection of RG domain walls is listed as an open problem in recent reviews.
